note: ORDER-FLOW ALIGNMENT GATE cohort (scripts/analyze_microstructure.py finding). Mining the 245k-row microstructure dataset showed top-5 order-book depth imbalance (depth_imb5) is the first genuinely directional signal in project history — and on the 329 live dev trades that had order-flow coverage, entries where the book AGREED with the trade won 37.2% vs 20.5% when it disagreed (~2x win-rate, ~half the per-trade loss). Still net-negative (the ~1.3bps signal sits under the ~4bps cost floor), so this is a risk-QUALITY filter, not an edge. This cohort forward-TESTS that lift live: momentum_continuation + mom_adx at 5m on exactly the 6 recorded pairs (BTC/ETH/SOL/DOGE/ADA/XRP), flow_gate_enabled=true with min_imbalance=0.0 (the measured aligned-vs-against split). The daemon (L3) reads the latest depth_imb5 snapshot and passes it to the pure detector gate; fail-closed when the feed is stale. Non-gate params match the fleet's risk-shaped profile so the GATE is the only variable. The ungated baseline momentum_continuation fleet is the implicit control — watch whether the cohort's live win-rate clears it. Backtest cannot evaluate this (no historical L2), which is exactly why it ships as a live forward-test arm.
